title: Shopping & Money
description: Prices, paying and change, bargaining at the market and buying online: the money words of everyday life in Indonesia.

items.registerNotes: Berapa harganya? (How much is it?) Harga pas is a fixed price with no bargaining, and harga mati a final, take-it-or-leave-it one.
Ada diskon? (Is there a discount?) suits shops, malls and apps; at a market you bargain instead.
Shop staff say Lagi promo for something on special right now. Beli satu gratis satu is buy one, get one free.

items.cultureNote: Small sellers often run short of change and ask Ada uang kecil? (Do you have anything smaller?), so carry small notes for warungs and ojeks.

items.registerNotes: Minta struknya, ya (Can I have the receipt?) A handwritten receipt is a nota, and a formal one for claims a kuitansi.
Bayar tunai is to pay cash, but people often just say cash: Bayar cash atau QRIS?

items.cultureNote: Paying by bank transfer is normal even for small things like kos rent or a homemade cake. Afterwards, send a screenshot as bukti transfer (proof of payment).

items.registerNotes: Bisa pakai kartu kredit? (Can I pay by credit card?) A debit card is a kartu debit, and paying by card is often just gesek (swipe).
Cicilan nol persen (0% instalments) is a common offer on phones and appliances, and dicicil means paid off in instalments.
Buka tabungan is to open a savings account. Menabung is to save money, and a piggy bank is a celengan.
Dompet digital is an e-wallet such as GoPay or OVO, used everywhere for small payments.
The official term is belanja daring, but hardly anyone says it.
items.cultureNote: Huge in Indonesia, through apps such as Shopee and Tokopedia. Many buyers choose COD, paying cash when the parcel arrives.

items.registerNotes: Short for ongkos kirim. Gratis ongkir (free delivery) is the commonest promise in online shopping.
In speech just kirim: Nanti saya kirim alamatnya (I'll send you the address). Sudah dikirim? asks whether an order has been sent, and the courier who brings it is the kurir.
A parcel in the post, but also a bundle: paket data (a mobile data plan), paket wisata (a package tour).
Ada ukuran yang lebih besar? (Do you have a bigger size?) Local clothing sizes run small, so try before you buy.

items.pitfallNote: More often a style or design than a fashion model: Modelnya bagus (Nice design). Ada model lain? asks for other styles.

items.cultureNote: Barang KW, from kualitas, are copies of brand-name goods, graded KW1, KW2 and so on. The real thing is ori (original).

items.registerNotes: Garansinya berapa lama? (How long is the warranty?) Keep the kartu garansi (warranty card) with the receipt.
Boleh tukar? (Can I exchange it?) for the wrong size, and tukar uang for changing money, at a money changer. Menukar is the written form.

items.english: to bargain, haggle; to make an offer
items.registerNotes: In speech nawar; Boleh ditawar? asks whether the price is open to bargaining. Bargain at markets and stalls, not in shops with price tags.
items.pitfallNote: Tawar on its own means plain or unsweetened: teh tawar is tea without sugar, and air tawar is fresh water.

items.registerNotes: Praise for good value: Makanannya murah meriah (The food is cheap and good).
For people and things: Dia hemat sekali (She's very careful with money), hemat listrik (saving electricity). Paket hemat is a value meal or bundle.
Jangan boros (Don't waste your money). It also describes things that use a lot: Motor ini boros bensin (This bike uses a lot of petrol).

items.cultureNote: Most phones are prepaid: you isi pulsa (top up) at a phone stall, a minimarket or in an app, then use it to buy a paket data.
